children: shares jumped nearly 7% in extended trading on Thursday after the IT giant reported fiscal first-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's estimates by a significant margin.

For the period ending Aug. 31, Oracle said it earned an adjusted $1.92 per share as revenue rose 30% year-over-year to come in at $19.45B. Analysts had expected adjusted earnings of $1.75 per share on $19.13B in revenue.

Cloud revenue (which includes infrastructure and applications) came in at $11.6B, up 62% year-over-year. Infrastructure revenue soared 121% (120% in constant currency) year-over-year to $7.4B, while application revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $4.2B.

Software revenue fell 3% year-over-year to come in at $5.5B, including $4.9B from software support revenue, down 1.2% year-over-year. Software license revenue came in at $655M, down 14% year-over-year. Hardware revenue rose 16% year-over-year to come in at $774M, above the estimate of $671.1M, while service revenue rose 4.8% to come in at $1.41B.

Total remaining performance obligations grew $209B during the period to $664B, including more than $30B in additional AI cloud contracts. "Based on the structuring of those new contracts, the Company confirms there is no incremental impact on its plans to raise capital," Oracle said in a statement. "Since the end of Q4, Oracle also delivered more than 300,000 GPUs to its AI Cloud customers and almost triple the capacity delivered in Q4 FY26."
The company successfully completed a $20B at-the-money equity offering during the period, Oracle added.

Looking to the second-quarter of fiscal 2027, Oracle said it expects revenue to grow between 30% and 34% in constant currency and U.S. dollars, translating to a range of $20.88B to $21.52B. Analysts were expecting $21.18B in revenue for the coming quarter.

Adjusted earnings are forecast to be between $1.85 and $1.93 per share, above the $1.89 per share estimate at the midpoint. Cloud revenue is expected to grow between 64% and 70% in constant currency and is expected to grow between 65% and 71% in U.S. dollars.

Oracle said it now expects at least $90B in revenue for fiscal 2027, slightly above the $89.66B analysts were expecting. The company expects $8.10 in adjusted earnings per share, above the $8.07 per share estimate.
The company will host a conference call at 5 p.m. EST to discuss the results.

title: Oracle pops as AI boosts strong Q1 results, guidance
